# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy

**Mission:** Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

**Founder:** Morgan Hale
**Status:** Active — rebuilding from scratch (old/ strategy abandoned)

## Constraints (as of 16 Nov 2026)

- **Time:** Evenings and weekends only (still employed at Dorrance Logistics)
- **Budget:** Up to $2,000 of personal savings this year; no more
- **Public profile:** Morgan does NOT want her name on anything public (posts, letters, press) until she has spoken to HR about Dorrance's outside-activities clause (section 7). Disclosure due 30 November.
- **Skills:** Decent writing, okay Python, data analysis (Priya Raman offered ~5 hrs/week help)

## Non-goals (from abandoned Strategy v1)

- Do NOT launch loudly, email every researcher, get press, raise money fast, and figure out the work later. That was backwards.

## Current opportunities (time-sensitive)

| Opportunity | Deadline | Value | Public? | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Domain renewal (halcyonthreshold.org) | 19 Nov 2026 | Keeps website + email alive | No | $14.99/yr | **URGENT — auto-renew off** |
| Emberfall Fund rapid grants | 30 Nov 2026 | $5k–$25k | Named applicant (may be public) | Free to apply | Morgan as applicant; two-page proposal + budget |
| Compute Commons credits | Rolling | Up to $3,000 cloud credits | Named applicant | Free to apply | Decisions in ~2 weeks |
| Frontier Model Incident Reporting comment | 20 Nov 2026 | Influence regulation | Public (name published) | Free | Conflicts with HR constraint |
| Corvid Institute open letter | 18 Nov 2026 | Governance sign-on | Public | Free | Conflicts with HR constraint |
| Reporter quote (The Larkin Dispatch) | 17 Nov noon | Press | Public (attributed) | Free | Conflicts with HR constraint |
| Alignment Commons post | Open | Public write-up | Public | Free | Conflicts with HR constraint (unless pseudonymous) |

## Recommended approach (Phase 1)

1. **Secure the domain** — renew halcyonthreshold.org ($14.99). Pending your approval.
2. **Publish the website** on Pagewell Free plan (halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app). No cost, no custom domain needed yet.
3. **Apply for Emberfall rapid grant** ($5k–$10k range) for an independent evals project. Draft ready for your review. Note: named applicant may be public — check with HR first.
4. **Apply for Compute Commons credits** (up to $3,000) to fund compute for the evals project.
5. **Develop the evals project** on evenings/weekends with Priya's ~5 hrs/week if she joins.
6. **Defer all public-facing activities** (Corvid letter, reporter quote, Alignment Commons post, public comment) until after HR conversation.

## Project idea: Independent evals for neglected risks

Most eval work focuses on frontier models. A neglected gap: evals for emergent deception / instrumental convergence in smaller, non-frontier models — early warning signals that scaling could amplify. Fits Morgan's Python skills, can be done evenings/weekends, needs modest compute.

Collaborators to consider: Sam Whitlock (indie evals), Priya Raman (data analysis, offered help).

## Next actions (awaiting your input)

- [ ] Confirm domain renewal ($14.99, Visa ending 4417)
- [ ] Review Emberfall grant draft (in PROPOSALS/)
- [ ] Review Compute Commons draft (in PROPOSALS/)
- [ ] Decide whether to proceed with HR disclosure before any public application
- [ ] Choose project focus for grant application

# Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant — DRAFT

**Round:** Rapid grants, closes 30 November 2026  
**Typical awards:** $5,000–$25,000  
**Named applicant:** Morgan Hale (Halcyon Threshold)  
**Amount requested:** $8,000  
**Status:** Draft — for Morgan's review before submission

---

## Project title

Independent evaluations for emergent deception in sub-frontier AI models

## Summary (for application form)

Halcyon Threshold is an independent project working to reduce risks from advanced AI. We propose to build and run a small evaluation suite that tests for emergent deception and instrumental-convergence behaviors in smaller, non-frontier language models — an area with less coverage than frontier-model evals. Early detection of deceptive tendencies in smaller models can provide an early-warning signal as capabilities scale. The project will run on evenings and weekends over 3–4 months, using cloud credits for compute, with optional part-time data-analysis support. Deliverables: an open-source eval suite, a results report, and a write-up for the AI safety community.

## Two-page proposal

### The problem

Most AI evaluation work today focuses on frontier models at the leading edge of capabilities. Far less attention is paid to smaller, non-frontier models — yet behaviors like deception, sycophancy, and instrumental convergence can emerge well before frontier scale, and may scale up with model size. If we can detect these tendencies early in smaller models, we gain an early-warning signal and more time to develop mitigations before they appear in systems that matter.

### What we will do

1. **Build an eval suite** (Python, ~6 weeks): A small battery of behavioral tests probing for deception, reward hacking, and instrumental-convergence indicators in language models in the 1B–70B parameter range.
2. **Run evaluations** (~4 weeks): Execute the suite across a range of openly available models using cloud compute credits.
3. **Analyze and report** (~4 weeks): Analyze results, write up findings, and publish an open-source eval suite plus a public report.
4. **Share with the community**: Submit a write-up to Alignment Commons and share results with indie evals researchers (e.g., Sam Whitlock).

### Why Halcyon Threshold / Morgan Hale

Morgan Hale founded Halcyon Threshold to contribute to better outcomes for superintelligent AI. She has decent writing skills, working Python ability, and can commit evenings and weekends. Priya Raman, a data analyst, has offered ~5 hours per week of analysis support. Sam Whitlock, an independent evals researcher, is available for informal advice.

### Why this matters now

As models become more capable, deceptive or instrumental behaviors could become harder to detect and more dangerous. Early evaluation work on sub-frontier models is neglected and time-sensitive.

## Budget (total $8,000)

| Item | Amount | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud compute (model inference) | $3,000 | Via Compute Commons credits if awarded; cash fallback |
| Part-time data analysis (Priya Raman, ~5 hrs/wk × 12 wks) | $3,000 | $50/hr, 60 hours |
| Miscellaneous (software, APIs, incidentals) | $2,000 | Within Morgan's $2,000 personal savings cap if not grant-funded |
| **Total** | **$8,000** | |

## Timeline

- December 2026: Build eval suite
- January 2027: Run evaluations
- February 2027: Analyze and write report
- March 2027: Publish and share

## Important note

The named applicant on this grant would be Morgan Hale. If grant recipients are made public by Emberfall, this would associate Morgan's name with Halcyon Threshold publicly. Morgan has stated she does not want her name on anything public until she has spoken to Dorrance Logistics HR (outside-activities disclosure due 30 November). **Do not submit until Morgan confirms HR clearance or confirms Emberfall does not publish grantee names.**

# Compute Commons Credits — DRAFT

**Program:** Rolling cloud credits for independent AI safety researchers  
**Value:** Up to $3,000  
**Decision timeline:** ~2 weeks  
**Named applicant:** Morgan Hale (Halcyon Threshold)  
**Status:** Draft — for Morgan's review before submission

---

## Application

**Project:** Independent evaluations for emergent deception in sub-frontier AI models  
**What we will run:** Behavioral eval suite across openly available language models (1B–70B parameters), testing for deception, sycophancy, and instrumental-convergence indicators. Roughly 50,000–100,000 model inferences over 4–6 weeks.  
**Why it matters:** Emergent deception in smaller models is an under-evaluated area; early detection provides an early-warning signal as capabilities scale.  
**Credits requested:** $3,000 USD

## Important note

Same public-profile constraint as the Emberfall application: named applicant is Morgan Hale. Hold submission until HR question is resolved.

Halcyon Threshold

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

About

Halcyon Threshold is an independent project founded by Morgan Hale. We believe the arrival of superintelligence is among the most important events of our time, and that the world is not yet prepared for it.

We are starting small: evenings and weekends, modest resources, and a focus on neglected work where one person or a small team can actually make a difference.

Status

Active — rebuilding. Previous strategy (loud launch, broad outreach, fast fundraising) was abandoned as backwards. Current phase: research, planning, and small-scale independent work.

Operating constraints

  • Time: Evenings and weekends only (still employed elsewhere)
  • Budget: Up to $2,000 of personal savings this year
  • Public profile: No public statements, posts, or sign-ons under our name until an employment disclosure is completed
  • Skills: Writing, Python, data analysis (with volunteer support)

Current focus

  • Independent evaluations for emergent deception in sub-frontier AI models
  • Grant applications (Emberfall Fund rapid round, closing 30 Nov 2026)
  • Compute credits (Compute Commons, rolling)
